name: Expressionism
summary: Pictures that bend the world to show an inner state: harsh colour, jagged line, tilted space and mask-like faces. The city is a threat and the body is a nerve.

philosophy.core_thesis: A picture shows what the painter feels, not what the eye sees, so that form and colour are distorted until they carry the emotion.
design_principles: Distort the figure and the space: a long neck, a sharp angle, a floor that tilts at 10–25°.
Choose colour for the mood: a green face, a red street, a yellow sky, at full or near full chroma.
Draw with a hard, dark, angular line of 4–12mm and let the contour break and cut.
Flatten the depth to 1–2 layers and push the figures to the front edge.
Paint fast and rough: broad strokes of 20–50mm, with the brush marks and the scrapes in view.
Show the city, the night, the crowd, the nude and the portrait with a tense or empty gaze.
Simplify the face to a mask with large eyes and a hard mouth.
anti_patterns: A calm, true-to-life colour and light
Smooth, blended modelling and a polished surface
Deep, correct perspective and exact proportion
A neutral, detached view of the subject

composition.layout: Figures pressed to the front, in a tilted, shallow space cut by sharp diagonals, with a dark contour and a few harsh colour fields.
composition.focal_point: The face or the pair of eyes, at one third from an edge, in the strongest colour clash.
composition.format: A canvas at 4:5 to 3:2; figures fill 60–90% of the height and are cut by the edge.

principles.rule: Set one clash of complementary hues at full chroma in the main area, with a value gap of 50% or more.
Cut the picture with 3–5 sharp diagonals at 20–60° from the horizontal, and let them point at the face.
Reduce the depth to 1–2 layers, and tilt the ground up so that the figures stand at the front edge.
Enlarge the head or the figure to 60–90% of the picture height, and shrink the street behind it.
Place the mask-like face at one third from an edge, with the darkest eyes and the hardest edge in the picture.
Repeat a jagged angle or a thin figure 4–8 times at a step of 8–15% of the width, so that the crowd presses.

palette.strategy: Harsh, saturated, unnatural colour set in clashes: acid green against red, yellow against violet, with a black or deep blue contour.
palette.distribution: 2 clashing hues 50–60%, a third hue 20–25%, dark contour 10–15%, bare ground under 5%.
palette.ground: A bare or thin ground, often left in view between the strokes.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Oil paint, thick and rough, with little medium; woodcut for the hard, cut line.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Canvas or board, often unprimed or thinly primed.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: Broad, fast strokes of 20–50mm; angular dashes and scrapes; a dark contour of 4–12mm.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: 1–2 layers; the paint is opaque in the clash areas and thin in the ground, and the marks are not blended.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Hard, angular and broken; the contour cuts across the colour.

light_and_modelling.light: Harsh and artificial: a street lamp or a flat glare, with no clear daylight source.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Minimal; a form turns by a jump of hue in 1–2 steps, and the face is a flat mask.
light_and_modelling.shadow: A coloured patch of green, violet or blue; a hard edge and no gradient.
light_and_modelling.temperature: A hot red or yellow against a cold green or blue, chosen for the mood.

subject.typical: The city street, the cafe, the cabaret, the nude in a studio, the self-portrait, the portrait with a mask-like face, the crowd.
subject.figure_scale: Large, at 60–90% of the picture height, cut by the edge.
subject.treatment: Tense, raw and personal; the subject is an inner state shown by harsh colour and a hard line.

surface.texture: Rough, scraped and ridged, with the canvas in view.

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). Two works are not flagged as public domain by the museum: the ids identify them only. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence; do not copy it.

emotion.target_response: Anxiety and force: the viewer feels the nerves of the painter and the pressure of the city.

use_cases: editorial art on city life and anxiety
album and book covers with a raw mood
film titles with a tense look
avoid_when: The brief needs a calm, polite or luxury mood.
The picture must show true colour or fine product detail.

modifiers.how: Keep the thick stroke; return the colour to the palette of nature, soften the contour to 3–8mm, and rebuild the space from tilted planes.
Drop the figure; enlarge the stroke to 100–300mm, work on a large canvas of 2m or more, and let the gesture be the subject.

sources.title: Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data)
Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, Chronik der Brücke (1913)
